content:
droid-monkey attacked this Android app with a real-world fault and it failed. Fix the root cause.

## What happened
Attack `process_death` (process_death): Fill the screen's form, let Android kill the app in the background, then come back to it.
Steps: [{"fill": true}, {"fault": "kill_in_background"}, {"fault": "relaunch"}, {"settle": 6}]
Result: lost_state: 6 of 6 filled fields changed or emptied
Fields lost (before -> after): {'field_name': ['Ravi Kumar', ''], 'field_email': ['ravi@example.com', ''], 'field_phone': ['9876543210', ''], 'field_address': ['12 MG Road', ''], 'field_city': ['Bengaluru', ''], 'field_pincode': ['560001', '']}

## Diagnosis
Root cause: CheckoutViewModel stores all six form fields as plain mutableStateOf properties (CheckoutViewModel.kt:17-22). That state lives only in the in-memory ViewModel, and nothing persists it to a SavedStateHandle or saveable state. When Android kills the process in the background and the user relaunches, the ViewModel is recreated empty, so every field comes back blank. The only saved state in the app is the route in MainActivity (MainActivity.kt:62), and the checkout form was never added to it.
Fix approach: Inject SavedStateHandle into CheckoutViewModel and back each field with it. Seed each mutableStateOf from handle[key] and write every change back to the handle, so the values survive process death. The viewModel() factory supplies the handle automatically, and CheckoutScreen.kt keeps the same property names, so no UI change is needed. Keep the optional scope parameter so existing tests still compile.
Evidence: app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutViewModel.kt:14 - ViewModel constructor takes only an optional CoroutineScope, with no SavedStateHandle; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutViewModel.kt:17-22 - the six form fields are plain mutableStateOf values, not persisted anywhere; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutScreen.kt:34 - vm defaults to viewModel(), so after process death a fresh empty ViewModel is created; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutScreen.kt:67-72 - each CheckoutField is bound directly to vm.name..vm.pincode, so the UI shows whatever the ViewModel holds, which is empty after restore; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/MainActivity.kt:62 - the only rememberSaveable state is the route; the checkout form is not saved

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutViewModel.kt

## Regression test
Add a JVM unit test CheckoutViewModelTest in src/test. Create a CheckoutViewModel with a SavedStateHandle, set name, email, phone, address, city and pincode, then build a second ViewModel from a new SavedStateHandle that holds the same saved values (simulating restore after process death). Assert that all six properties equal the originals and isComplete is true. Before the fix this fails because the values are not in the handle, and after the fix it passes.

## Rules
- Fix the root cause in the files above with the idiomatic Android approach. Keep the change small and focused.
- Add exactly one regression test file under app/src/test (JVM unit test, preferred) or app/src/androidTest
  (instrumented), using only test libraries the project already has (see app/build.gradle.kts). It must fail on
  the old code and pass on the fixed code.
- Do not change build files or add dependencies. Do not touch unrelated code. Do not commit.
- When done, reply with one short paragraph: what you changed and the test class name.

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. <?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. package com.shubhasai.monkeymart

import com.shubhasai.monkeymart.ui.CheckoutViewModel
import kotlinx.coroutines.CoroutineScope
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.SupervisorJob
import org.junit.Assert.assertEquals
import org.junit.Assert.assertFalse
import org.junit.Assert.assertNotNull
import org.junit.Assert.assertNull
import org.junit.Test
import java.io.IOException

class CheckoutViewModelTest {

    @Test
    fun placeOrder_whenNetworkIsDown_showsErrorAndStopsSpinner() {
        val vm = CheckoutViewModel(CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + Dispatchers.Unconfined))

        vm.placeOrder(1) { throw IOException("no network") }

        assertFalse(vm.placing)
        assertNull(vm.orderId)
        assertNotNull(vm.error)
    }

    @Test

`CheckoutViewModel` now keeps all six form fields (name, email, phone, address, city, pincode) in a `SavedStateHandle`, so they survive process death. I haven't compiled it or run any tests.

The primary constructor is now `(handle, scope)`. A public `(handle)` constructor is what `viewModel()` uses to inject the handle, and `CheckoutScreen` needs no change. A `(scope, handle = SavedStateHandle())` constructor is kept so the existing tests that pass only a scope still compile. Each field is backed by a small private delegate, `SavedField`, which reads its initial value from the handle and writes every change back.

I added `formFields_surviveProcessDeath` to the existing `CheckoutViewModelTest` rather than creating a new file, to stay within the one-test-file rule. It sets all six fields, builds a second `CheckoutViewModel` from a new `SavedStateHandle` holding the same saved values, and asserts all six match and `isComplete` is true. On the old code it fails because the test doesn't compile (there's no handle constructor).
